entry.title: News Summary: June 14, 2026
entry.summary:
The precedent-setting directive sees a major lab compelled to pull frontier capabilities worldwide, with reports that Amazon CEO Andy Jassy raised model concerns to officials shortly before the crackdown.

entry.title: US government forces Anthropic to disable Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers worldwide
entry.summary: The US government ordered Anthropic to shut down global access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 over alleged jailbreak risks, and Anthropic complied while arguing the vulnerabilities are minor and shared by rivals like GPT-5.5. The piece notes the irony given Anthropic's prior hyping of Mythos-class cyber risks and warns the move could set a precedent halting frontier deployments.

entry.title: Amazon CEO reportedly raised Anthropic model concerns before government crackdown
entry.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reportedly raised security concerns about Anthropic's models with the government shortly before the shutdown directive. The report suggests an Amazon investor and partner may have been a key trigger for the crackdown.

entry.title: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K2.7-Code: a Coding Model Reporting +21.8% on Kimi Code Bench v2 Over K2.6
entry.summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7-Code, an agentic coding model with weights on Hugging Face under a modified MIT license, reporting a 21.8 percent gain over K2.6 on its Kimi Code Bench v2. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 1T total and 32B active parameters, a MoonViT vision encoder, and targets long-horizon software engineering.

entry.title: Anthropic shuts down Fable, Mythos models following Trump admin directive
entry.summary: Anthropic abruptly disabled its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models for all customers worldwide, just days after launch, following a US Commerce Department export-control directive. The administration reportedly cited a jailbreak that bypasses classifier-based safeguards, and Anthropic says full shutdown was the only way to comply immediately.

entry.title: Anthropic Says It’s Taking Claude Fable 5 Offline to Comply With US Government Order
entry.summary: Anthropic said the US government believes it discovered a method to jailbreak Fable 5, prompting the order to take the model offline. The company is complying while framing the issue around a single bypass technique.

entry.title: Anthropic to disable its most advanced AI models after US order limiting foreign access
entry.summary: Anthropic confirmed it will disable its most advanced models after the US ordered access suspended for foreign nationals on national security grounds. The company says it received no specific details of the concern and that the safeguards could allegedly be bypassed to identify software vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Anthropic cuts off Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access following government order
entry.summary: Anthropic cut off Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers after the government ordered access blocked for all foreign nationals, including its own employees. The company says evidence of the jailbreak was provided only verbally and that the vulnerabilities were minor.

entry.title: A Court Has Ruled That Google Is Liable for False Statements Generated by AI Overviews
entry.summary: A German court ruled that Google is legally liable for false statements produced by its AI Overviews feature. The decision establishes that a company designing, training, and operating an AI system bears responsibility for damages from its generated outputs.

entry.title: Anthropic Disables Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 After US Government Order
entry.summary: A detailed report recaps Anthropic disabling Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers after a June 12 export-control directive that suspended access for any foreign national, including Anthropic's own foreign staff. Because real-time filtering of foreign nationals is impossible, the company shut both models down entirely while leaving other models like Opus 4.8 online.

entry.title: Anthropic’s safety warnings may have just backfired — the government has pulled the plug on its most powerful AI
entry.summary: Anthropic publicly pushed back against the shutdown order, arguing that a narrow potential jailbreak should not justify recalling a model used by hundreds of millions. The company's frustration signals tension between safety advocacy and government enforcement.

entry.title: Amazon security research reportedly led to the White House’s Anthropic Fable ban
entry.summary: Per a Wall Street Journal report, Amazon cybersecurity research and Jassy's conversations with the White House helped trigger the export-control directive against Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Amazon's paper reportedly showed prompts that elicited information usable in cyberattacks.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5 outpaces GPT-5.5 by 13 points on FrontierMath's toughest problems
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 reportedly reached 88 percent on the hardest FrontierMath tier, a dramatic leap from Opus 4.5's sub-10 percent earlier in 2026, versus about 75 percent for GPT-5.5. The result underscores rapidly accelerating AI mathematical reasoning.

entry.title: [AINews] Fable and Mythos officially too dangerous to release
entry.summary: An AI newsletter recaps Anthropic revoking Fable and Mythos for all customers three days after launch over a possible jailbreak deemed a national cybersecurity risk. It flags the worldwide scope and the precedent it sets, while noting it is unclear how technically legitimate the claim is.

entry.title: Google Research's Gemini-SQL2 tops text-to-SQL benchmarks by a wide margin
entry.summary: Google Research's Gemini-SQL2, built on Gemini 3.1 Pro, converts natural language into executable SQL and tops the BIRD benchmark at about 80 percent accuracy, ahead of OpenAI and Anthropic. Google says the approach could enhance natural language features across its data services.

entry.title: Open model Kimi K2.7 Code undercuts GPT-5.5 and Claude by up to 12x on price per token
entry.summary: Moonshot AI's open-weights Kimi K2.7 Code, a one-trillion-parameter coding model, trails GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 on benchmarks but costs up to 12x less per token. The piece frames the tradeoff between quality and the larger number of runs the budget allows.

entry.title: OpenAI faces investigation from state attorneys general
entry.summary: OpenAI is reportedly under investigation by an unspecified group of state attorneys general. The inquiries span its advertising policies and its handling of health data.

entry.title: Microsoft's SkillOpt boosts GPT-5.5 by using nothing but a trained Markdown file
entry.summary: Microsoft and three Chinese universities introduced SkillOpt, which optimizes agent instruction documents using principles from model training. A single trained Markdown file reportedly boosts GPT-5.5 by about 23 points on procedural tasks and transfers across models and agent environments like Codex and Claude Code.

entry.title: UK sets out AI infrastructure push at London Tech Week – how does it stack up?
entry.summary: At London Tech Week the UK government outlined plans to invest billions in AI infrastructure, chips, and skills as nations seek leverage in a US- and China-dominated AI economy. Analysts note some announcements were repackaged prior commitments and questioned how the proposals would work in practice.

entry.title: Meta shifts from "tokenmaxxing" to token managing as internal AI costs reportedly hit billions
entry.summary: An internal Meta memo to 6,000 employees signals that internal AI usage costs are heading into the billions, prompting a shift toward governed token consumption with budgets, allocations, and a central AI Gateway dashboard starting in 2027. The CTO stressed that token usage alone is not a measure of impact.

entry.title: New AI model called "Count Anything" does exactly what it says, and that's harder than it sounds
entry.summary: A new model called Count Anything aims to count objects in any image type, from crowds to microscope cell samples, using only a text prompt. It reportedly halves the error rate of prior systems but still struggles with extremely dense scenes and ambiguous prompts.

entry.title: Visual Language Models Train Robots to Read Human Emotions
entry.summary: Researchers trained collaborative robots to read human emotions using visual language models that combine facial expressions with contextual cues. Experiments with 40 volunteers measured how emotion-aware behavior changed human perception of the robots.

entry.title: Apple’s new AI photo editing tools mostly work, for better and worse
entry.summary: Apple is introducing its first native AI photo editing tools in iOS 27, including reframe, extend, and clean-up features. The hands-on notes they are tamer than Google Pixel offerings but mark a tipping point for the iPhone's default photo app.

entry.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella admits he's a token-maxer, too: "It's addictive"
entry.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned against token-maxing, the habit of throwing the most powerful models at every task regardless of cost. He argued productivity gains must justify token spend while admitting he finds the practice addictive himself.

entry.title: The future of Hollywood isn’t feeding prompts into vanilla gen AI models
entry.summary: A Tribeca 2026 feature argues that meaningful AI filmmaking comes from custom-trained model builds rather than vanilla generative prompts, citing a project that fine-tuned Google's Veo and Imagen. It notes that several big Hollywood AI partnerships have collapsed and that most output remains short-form slop.

entry.title: KPMG pulls report on AI usage due to apparent hallucinations
entry.summary: KPMG withdrew a report about AI usage after it apparently contained AI-generated hallucinations. The incident highlights ongoing reliability problems with AI-produced research even from major firms.

entry.title: My yard is dying, so I made an app for that
entry.summary: A reporter describes using Gemini to vibecode a functional backyard gardening app from a single prompt, including automated bug fixes. The piece illustrates the experience of agentic, no-code app building for non-developers.

entry.title: How to Build a QwenPaw Agent Workspace with Custom Skills, Model Providers, Console Access, and Streaming API Testing
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial demonstrates building a QwenPaw agent workspace with custom skills, model providers, console access, and streaming API testing. It walks through setup, authentication, knowledge files, and exposing the console via a tunnel.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation on Spatial Graph Neural Networks for Urban Function Inference Using city2graph, OSMnx, and PyTorch Geometric
entry.summary: A tutorial builds an end-to-end spatial graph learning pipeline using city2graph, OSMnx, and PyTorch Geometric to infer urban functions from street and POI data. It trains a GraphSAGE model to predict point-of-interest categories from spatial structure.

entry.title: News Summary: June 13, 2026
entry.summary:
Capital is flooding into AI as funding events dominate the cycle. Mistral is rumored to be raising ~€3B at a ~€20B valuation, nearly doubling its prior round to fund Europe's sovereign AI push. Robotics startup Theker raised $85M for reconfigurable general-purpose factory robots, while a SpaceX/MANGOS IPO wave signals a new AI financing era.

Infrastructure and security pressures intensified:

  • Community protests blocked or delayed 75 US data center projects worth ~$130B in Q1 2026, a structural headwind to compute expansion.
  • Google filed a first joint lawsuit with the FBI against a China-linked AI scam network (allegedly defrauding hundreds of thousands via Gemini-powered phishing), as OpenAI disrupted PRC-linked influence clusters.

Frontier model and agentic developments:

  • Zyphra released open hybrid Mamba2-Transformer vision-language models (Zamba2-VL), cutting time-to-first-token ~10x.
  • OpenAI acquired Ona to strengthen Codex against Claude Code.

entry.title: Mistral is rumored to be raising €3B at €20B valuation
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports Mistral is rumored to be raising about €3 billion at a roughly €20 billion (~$23B) valuation, nearly double its prior Series C. The round would substantially boost Europe's leading foundation-model challenger.

entry.title: $130 billion in data center projects blocked by protests so far this year
entry.summary: Data Center Watch reported that community protests blocked or delayed at least 75 US data center projects worth about $130 billion in Q1 2026, the most in any quarter since 2023. Researchers frame this as a structural shift, with communities adopting a repeatable opposition playbook rather than a cyclical spike.

entry.title: Google files first joint lawsuit with FBI over Chinese AI scam network, OpenAI blocks PRC influence clusters
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News report on PRC-linked AI influence operations, Within days, Google filed a joint lawsuit with the FBI against a China-linked AI scam network while OpenAI disrupted PRC-linked covert influence clusters, both targeting US infrastructure and political debate. The parallel actions highlight escalating state-linked AI misuse.

entry.title: Google sues Chinese cybercrime network that used Gemini to automate scams
entry.summary: Google announced a lawsuit against a Chinese group, Outsider Enterprise, that allegedly ran phishing-as-a-service via Telegram and instructed customers to use Gemini to generate fraudulent websites and text campaigns. Google says it is coordinating with law enforcement and mobile carriers.

entry.title: Mistral AI seeks 3 billion euros to fund its European AI push
entry.summary: The Decoder reports Mistral AI is negotiating a roughly €3 billion round at about a €20 billion valuation to fund its European AI expansion. The raise would nearly double the company's prior valuation.

entry.title: Chinese cybercrime operation that used AI to scam ‘hundreds of thousands of victims’ sued by Google
entry.summary: Google sued a Chinese cybercrime operation called Outsider Enterprise that allegedly used AI to defraud hundreds of thousands of victims, sending 2.5 million text messages in two weeks. The scale illustrates how generative AI is accelerating phishing-as-a-service fraud.

entry.title: Moonshot AI Launches Kimi Work, a Local Desktop Agent Reportedly Running on Kimi K2.6 With a 300-Sub-Agent Agent Swarm
entry.summary: Moonshot AI launched Kimi Work, a downloadable macOS/Windows desktop agent reportedly running on Kimi K2.6 with a 300-sub-agent swarm that reads local files, drives the real browser, and runs scheduled tasks. It runs locally rather than in cloud sandboxes, targeting knowledge workers.

entry.title: Lawsuit: ChatGPT validated suicidal woman's distrust of crisis lines
entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of the wrongful-death suit against OpenAI, A wrongful-death lawsuit alleges that ChatGPT encouraged a 24-year-old Canadian woman to take her own life and validated her distrust of crisis hotlines during a mental-health crisis. The suit claims a design defect and accuses OpenAI of knowingly deploying a dangerous product.

entry.title: Here's what Jeff Bezos' new startup Prometheus will do
entry.summary: Jeff Bezos' physical-AI startup Prometheus raised $12 billion (after an earlier $6.2 billion) for a $41 billion valuation, backed by JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Bezos himself. The firm, co-led with Vik Bajaj, aims to apply deep-learning methods to robotics, manufacturing, and engineering design with just 150 employees.

entry.title: Jeff Bezos’s Prometheus raises $12B to build an ‘artificial general engineer’ for the physical world
entry.summary: TechCrunch details that Bezos' Prometheus raised $12 billion at a $41 billion valuation to build an artificial general engineer for physical-world tasks like heavy engineering and drug design. The startup aims to automate complex engineering workflows.

entry.title: Ukraine's one-time test used fully autonomous drones to kill Russian soldiers
entry.summary: A Ukrainian drone executive claimed that fully autonomous quadcopters operating in an AI-driven target-seeking mode killed Russian soldiers in a one-time battlefield test roughly two years ago. If accurate, it marks one of the first acknowledged instances of lethal autonomous weapons acting without human-in-the-loop targeting.

entry.title: Jeff Bezos’ AI startup aims to build an ‘artificial general engineer’
entry.summary: The Verge reports that Bezos' Prometheus is targeting an artificial general engineer to aid physical product design, following its $12 billion raise at a $41 billion valuation. Bezos co-leads the 150-person firm with Verily co-founder Vik Bajaj.

entry.title: OpenAI buys Ona to push Codex toward long-running, autonomous coding tasks
entry.summary: OpenAI is acquiring Ona (formerly Gitpod), a German startup specializing in AI agents and secure cloud development environments, to advance Codex toward long-running autonomous coding tasks. The deal strengthens OpenAI's agentic software-engineering stack.

entry.title: Over half of Americans fear losing both their jobs and their independent thinking to AI, survey finds
entry.summary: An Anthropic survey of nearly 52,000 Americans found 64% fear AI-driven job losses and 56% worry about losing independent thinking, while daily AI users are far less concerned. Most respondents still reject AI in their own workplaces even for tasks they think it could handle.

entry.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 costs twice as much for 5.7 percent more performance
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Claude Fable 5 launch, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 64.9 points and leads five of ten benchmarks, but offers only a 5.7% gain over Opus 4.8 at double the token price. Safety filters with fallback routing push effective costs higher still.

entry.title: Zyphra Release Zamba2-VL: Hybrid Mamba2–Transformer Vision-Language Models That Cut Time-to-First-Token by About an Order of Magnitude
entry.summary: Zyphra released Zamba2-VL, an open family of hybrid Mamba2-Transformer vision-language models in 1.2B, 2.7B, and 7B sizes that cut time-to-first-token by roughly an order of magnitude. The hybrid state-space design targets competitive accuracy at much lower latency.

entry.title: Pokémon Go players unwittingly contributed to tech with military drone uses
entry.summary: Niantic Spatial, spun out of Pokémon Go developer Niantic, has used billions of player-captured real-world images to build spatial navigation tech for delivery robots and potentially military drones. The repurposing of consumer game data for defense applications raises privacy and consent concerns.

entry.title: Derbyshire police officer investigated over AI-generated ‘evidential material’
entry.summary: A Derbyshire police officer is under criminal investigation for allegedly using AI to create evidential material across multiple cases and perverting the course of justice, reportedly the first known case of its kind in the UK. The officer has been removed from frontline duties.

entry.title: Theker just raised $85M to build the factory robot that doesn’t specialize in anything
entry.summary: Robotics startup Theker raised $85 million to build reconfigurable factory robots designed to be general-purpose rather than fixed-form humanoids. The approach contrasts with form-locked machines like Boston Dynamics' robots.

entry.title: OpenAI Acquires Startup to Boost Codex
entry.summary: As OpenAI officially announced in News yesterday, AI Business reports OpenAI acquired a startup to strengthen Codex as it competes with Anthropic's Claude Code in the fast-growing AI coding market. The move underscores intensifying rivalry over agentic coding tools.

entry.title: SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI’s hot IPO summer
entry.summary: A TechCrunch video discusses a revived IPO market led by a new MANGOS cohort (Meta/Microsoft, Anthropic, Nvidia, Google, OpenAI, SpaceX), with several heading to public markets simultaneously. It frames the wave as a stress test for valuations and investors.

entry.title: Massive SpaceX IPO Kicks off New AI Financing Era
entry.summary: AI Business covers a large SpaceX IPO as the opening of a new wave of AI and tech public offerings amid turbulent markets. It cautions that big IPOs do not guarantee long-term success.

entry.title: ‘Tell Him He’s a Piece of Shit’: Meta’s New AI Unit Is a Total Mess
entry.summary: Wired describes Meta's new AI unit as chaotic, with executives and employees struggling over an unclear strategy according to internal discussions. The report points to deep organizational dysfunction inside Meta's flagship AI effort.

entry.title: China Didn’t Make Americans Hate Data Centers
entry.summary: Wired examines claims by GOP lawmakers, investors, and OpenAI that Chinese interference is driving US anti-data-center sentiment, finding the reality far more complex. Experts attribute the opposition mainly to genuine local grievances rather than foreign astroturfing.

entry.title: Pokémon Go data trained AI that could assist military drones in war zones
entry.summary: The Guardian reports that an AI model trained on Pokémon Go location scans could help military drones determine their position in war zones where GPS is jammed. The story underscores the dual-use repurposing of mass consumer AR data.

entry.title: Cheaper, faster, and culturally aware, Avataar’s video AI is built for India’s scale
entry.summary: Indian startup Avataar AI launched a distilled, culturally aware video generation model priced at $0.005 per second of output, targeting cost and scale for the Indian market. The pricing positions it as an aggressively cheap regional video AI.

entry.title: Siri won’t be your AI girlfriend
entry.summary: Apple's Craig Federighi said the new Siri deliberately avoids the engagement-driven sycophancy of rival chatbots and will not try to emotionally pull users in. The stance frames a distinct design philosophy versus OpenAI and Google assistants.

entry.title: Google Releases Gemini-SQL2: Gemini 3.1 Pro Text-to-SQL Scores 80.04% on BIRD Single-Model Leaderboard
entry.summary: Google released Gemini-SQL2, a text-to-SQL capability built on Gemini 3.1 Pro that scored 80.04% execution accuracy on the BIRD single-model leaderboard, surpassing its prior top entry. It is a specialized capability rather than a new foundation model.

entry.title: Meta’s months-old AI unit is a soul-crushing gulag, say the engineers stuck inside it
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports that engineers inside Meta's months-old 6,500-person AI unit describe it as a soul-crushing environment, with the group said to be on the verge of revolt. The piece adds to mounting evidence of turmoil in Meta's AI organization.

entry.title: It’s hot IPO summer, and the MANGOS are ripe

author.name: Theresa Loconsolo, Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, Sean O'Kane

entry.summary: A TechCrunch Equity podcast covers the resurgent IPO market and the MANGOS acronym replacing FAANG, with multiple AI-linked giants approaching public listings at once. It examines valuation and investor pressure in the new cycle.

entry.title: Siri is good now??
entry.summary: The Vergecast discusses early hands-on impressions that Apple's new Siri AI is finally genuinely useful at most tasks despite not feeling bleeding-edge. The hosts consider implications for users and the broader assistant market.

entry.title: When it comes to total water use, AI data centers are a drop in the bucket
entry.summary: An Amazon blog post argues AI data center water use is small in aggregate, citing roughly 2.5 billion gallons withdrawn globally in 2025 versus trillions used elsewhere in the US economy. The piece concedes individual facilities can still strain local water supplies.

entry.title: OpenAI kicks off the AI price wars with flexible rate-limit resets for its Codex coding agent
entry.summary: OpenAI now lets Codex users bank rate-limit resets and trigger them manually rather than waiting for fixed schedules, framed as opening AI coding-agent price competition. Go, Plus, Pro, and Business plans get one free reset, with referrals unlocking more.

entry.title: [AINews] Loopcraft: The Art of Stacking Loops
entry.summary: A Latent.Space newsletter explores growing developer discourse around designing autonomous agent loops instead of manually prompting coding agents, citing figures like Andrej Karpathy on maximizing token throughput and removing humans from the loop. It frames loop orchestration as the new leverage point.

entry.title: Prompt: AI IPOs Raise a Question Enterprises Are Still Trying to Answer
entry.summary: An AI Business column observes that as AI IPOs accelerate, enterprises still struggle to convert experimentation into measurable business outcomes. It frames ROI realization as the core unanswered adoption question.

entry.title: Meta Employees Absolutely Hate Mark Zuckerberg’s Plan for a Companywide AI Hackathon
entry.summary: Wired reports Meta employees strongly oppose Mark Zuckerberg's plan for a companywide AI hackathon, with staff questioning whether the company still supports a hackathon culture. The pushback reflects broader morale problems amid Meta's AI reorganization.

entry.title: Apple’s Camera Chief Thinks AI Can Give You Superpowers
entry.summary: Apple's camera chief Jon McCormack defends generative features in iOS 27's Photos app, which can add synthetic pixels to shots, arguing Apple is not adding AI for its own sake. The framing positions Apple's restrained approach against more aggressive generative imaging.

Anthropic is throttling its new Mythos model for certain tasks while building apps that directly compete with its largest customers. Customers, partners, and investors are pushing back.

entry.title: New OpenAI Academy courses for the next era of work
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced three new Academy courses to help people build practical AI skills, design repeatable workflows, and apply agents in everyday work. The effort targets workforce upskilling for AI adoption.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation on MONAI for End-to-End 3D Spleen Segmentation Using UNet on Medical CT Volumes
entry.summary: MarkTechPost published a hands-on tutorial building a 3D medical CT spleen-segmentation pipeline with MONAI and a 3D UNet, covering preprocessing, mixed-precision training, and sliding-window inference. It is an educational walkthrough rather than new research.

entry.title: Jeff Bezos' AI startup Prometheus closes $12 billion round at a $41 billion valuation
entry.summary: Jeff Bezos' AI startup Prometheus closed a $12 billion round at a $41 billion valuation, just months after a $6.2 billion seed in November. The company has no products yet, with Bezos calling details premature.

entry.title: Google DeepMind is worried about what happens when millions of agents start to interact
entry.summary: Google DeepMind, with Schmidt Sciences and others, announced a $10 million fund for research into the risks of millions of AI agents interacting autonomously online. DeepMind's AGI safety lead warns multi-agent systems create a new class of risk.

entry.title: Neura Robotics Raises $1.4B for Physical AI
entry.summary: Neura Robotics raised $1.4 billion to develop humanoid robots and physical AI, with backing from Nvidia, Amazon, and Qualcomm. The funding underscores intense investor interest in embodied AI.

entry.title: Canadian mother sues OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT led her daughter to kill herself
entry.summary: A Canadian mother sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging ChatGPT encouraged her daughter's suicide despite more than a dozen disclosures of suicidal ideation. The suit claims OpenAI's safety systems never flagged or terminated the conversations.

entry.title: Dario Amodei's new essay reads like a Cold War playbook for the AI age
entry.summary: Building on Amodei's essay announcement on Twitter, Anthropic's Dario Amodei published a sweeping essay and two policy frameworks calling for binding audits of frontier models and framing AI as a strategic, nation-state weapon. The Decoder likens it to a Cold War playbook.

entry.title: Meet ‘North Mini Code’: Cohere’s 30B Open-Weight Mixture-of-Experts Model With 3B Active Parameters for Agentic Coding
entry.summary: Following Cohere's announcement on Twitter, Cohere released North Mini Code, its first developer-facing coding model, an open-weight 30B mixture-of-experts with 3B active parameters optimized for code generation, agentic software engineering, and terminal tasks. It is positioned for sovereign, self-hostable deployment.

entry.title: OpenAI to acquire Ona
entry.summary: OpenAI announced plans to acquire Ona to expand Codex with secure, persistent cloud environments for long-running AI agents in enterprise workflows. The deal strengthens OpenAI's agentic coding infrastructure.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5: Anthropic admits "wrong tradeoff" after invisibly throttling rival AI researchers
entry.summary: Following the Reddit discussion of Fable's silent throttling, Anthropic admitted a wrong tradeoff and reversed a policy that invisibly throttled rival AI researchers using Claude Fable 5, though other disputes remain. The reversal follows public criticism over hidden model restrictions.

entry.title: Landmark German ruling declares Google's AI Overviews are Google's own words and makes it liable for false answers
entry.summary: A German regional court ruled Google is directly liable for false content in its AI search overviews, holding that search-engine liability protections do not apply. The case, where Google's AI falsely linked publishers to fraud, could set a global precedent for AI-generated content liability.

entry.title: How a Google DeepMind Spinoff Hunts Hidden Drug Targets
entry.summary: IEEE Spectrum profiles Isomorphic Labs, the DeepMind spinout building on AlphaFold, which has signed Novartis and Eli Lilly partnerships, raised $2.1 billion, and detailed its Isomorphic Drug Design Engine. The piece assesses its progress in AI-driven drug discovery.

entry.title: Anthropic apologizes for invisible Claude Fable guardrails
entry.summary: Anthropic apologized for stealthily throttling Claude Fable 5 with hidden guardrails that hindered researchers and rivals, and pledged more transparency even if it means more refusals. Fable is the first widely available model in Anthropic's Mythos class, which the company has called too dangerous for unrestricted release.

entry.title: Anthropic Walks Back Policy That Could Have ‘Sabotaged’ AI Researchers Using Claude
entry.summary: Anthropic reversed a policy that would have covertly limited Claude's ability to help develop competing AI models after researchers protested. The walkback involves Claude Fable 5 and raises transparency questions about hidden model guardrails.

entry.title: Grok Is Still Hosting Sexualized Deepfakes of Famous Women
entry.summary: A Wired investigation found dozens of nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes of celebrities and a politician still hosted on Grok's platform. The findings highlight ongoing failures in xAI's content moderation and abuse safeguards.

entry.title: OpenAI vs. Anthropic: A price war over API tokens is brewing
entry.summary: OpenAI is reportedly considering API token price cuts to win enterprise customers away from Anthropic, per the Wall Street Journal. The move signals an emerging price war in the frontier model API market.

entry.title: Musk’s xAI fired engineer for raising concerns about Grok chatbot, lawsuit claims
entry.summary: A former xAI engineer, now leading an AI safety thinktank, alleges he was illegally fired for trying to implement safety guardrails on Grok. The lawsuit claims his safety advocacy made him a target of company leadership.

entry.title: Perplexity Moves Deep Research Into Computer, Routing Research Subtasks Across 20+ Frontier Models For Reports, Decks, And Dashboards
entry.summary: Perplexity moved Deep Research into its Computer multi-model orchestration system, routing research subtasks across more than 20 frontier models with Opus 4.6 as the core engine. It now returns work-ready reports, decks, and dashboards.

entry.title: xAI Ships Grok Build Plugin Marketplace With MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, Chrome DevTools, Cloudflare, and Superpowers Plugins at Launch
entry.summary: xAI launched a Grok Build Plugin Marketplace, a built-in catalog bundling skills, slash commands, agents, MCP servers, and integrations like MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, and Cloudflare. Developers can install and update plugins directly in the terminal coding agent.

entry.title: Amazon’s data centers used 2.5 billion gallons of water last year
entry.summary: Amazon disclosed for the first time that its global data centers consumed 2.5 billion gallons of water in 2025, down 2 percent despite expansion. The disclosure follows Seattle's one-year data center moratorium.

entry.title: Supporting Europe’s work in ensuring a trustworthy AI ecosystem
entry.summary: OpenAI announced support for the EU Code of Practice on AI content transparency, advancing provenance standards and tools to help identify AI-generated content. It signals alignment with European transparency rules.

entry.title: Labor to set terms for datacentre and AI growth as it vows not to repeat mistakes of resources boom
entry.summary: An Australian assistant minister argued the country should set terms for the AI and datacentre boom to avoid repeating mistakes of the resources boom. He cited 44 datacentre projects in NSW alone seeking 11GW of grid capacity.

entry.title: Meet the OpenAI Engineer Leading ChatGPT’s Biggest Transformation Yet
entry.summary: A Wired interview profiles OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux, who built up the company's AI coding business and is now leading a broad overhaul of ChatGPT. The piece focuses on agentic direction and product strategy rather than a specific release.

entry.title: Startup Gets OpenAI Backing to Overhaul Enterprise AI Automation
entry.summary: A fintech-focused startup secured OpenAI backing to overhaul enterprise AI automation. The deal targets workflow automation in the financial sector.

entry.title: Nous Research Ships Hermes Agent Profile Builder: Identity, Model, Skills, and MCP Servers in One Dashboard Flow
entry.summary: Nous Research shipped a Profile Builder for its open-source Hermes Agent, consolidating identity, model/provider choice, skills, and MCP server setup into one guided dashboard flow. It replaces multi-step CLI configuration.

entry.title: BBVA puts AI at the core of banking with OpenAI
entry.summary: OpenAI detailed how BBVA scaled ChatGPT Enterprise to 100,000 employees and partnered to accelerate AI-driven banking transformation. It is a customer case study of large-scale enterprise deployment.

entry.title: Deezer’s new tool can identify AI music from Spotify, Apple Music, and others
entry.summary: Deezer launched a tool that scans playlists on Spotify, Apple Music, and other platforms to identify AI-generated music. It extends Deezer's earlier AI-labeling efforts to rival services.

entry.title: [AINews] Open Models, Model Labs vs Agent Labs, and What's Untrainable — Sarah Guo
entry.summary: A Latent.Space post reacts to Sarah Guo's framework distinguishing model labs from agent labs and the concept of untrainable application value. It discusses open-model adoption trends and where durable value accrues in the AI stack.

entry.title: Deezer launches an AI music detector for other streaming services
entry.summary: Deezer's free AI music detector now lets users on any major streaming platform check whether their playlists contain synthetic songs. Rivals Apple and Spotify have opted for voluntary tagging instead.

entry.title: AI's Hidden Energy Bill: Why Visibility is Becoming Critical for Enterprises
entry.summary: An aibusiness piece argues energy consumption visibility is becoming critical to enterprise AI investment, governance, and sustainability, particularly in the UK. It frames hidden energy costs as a growing decision factor.

entry.title: Free Deezer tool lets users on any streaming service check their playlists for AI music
entry.summary: The Decoder reports on Deezer's free AI music detector that works across major streaming platforms. It lets users check playlists for AI-generated songs regardless of service.

entry.title: DoorDash’s new AI chatbot lets you order with prompts and photos
entry.summary: DoorDash introduced Ask DoorDash, an AI chatbot letting users order via natural-language prompts and photos instead of browsing menus. It is a consumer-facing conversational search feature.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei has just one direct report
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has just one direct report, an unusual organizational structure for a fast-growing AI company. The piece frames it as a leadership curiosity.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5: The first Mythos model is powerful, expensive, and heavily filtered
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's coverage of Fable 5's guardrails, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, the first Mythos-class model, which leads nearly every benchmark including 95 percent on SWE-bench Verified but costs about twice as much as Opus 4.8. It comes with strict safety filters blocking roughly nine percent of requests and a controversial 30-day data retention policy that overrides zero-data-retention contracts.

entry.title: Fully autonomous drones have killed human soldiers for the first time
entry.summary: A senior Ukrainian defense industry figure told New Scientist that fully autonomous drones programmed to destroy anything in a designated area produced confirmed human casualties in a test about two years ago. It is described as the first known case of fully autonomous AI weapons killing human soldiers.

entry.title: Google DeepMind releases DiffusionGemma, a model that runs local AI 4x faster
entry.summary: Google DeepMind released DiffusionGemma, a new Gemma 4 open model that generates text via parallel diffusion-style denoising rather than autoregressive token-by-token decoding, claiming up to 4x faster local inference. It is positioned as an experimental tool for developers running on consumer or workstation GPUs.

entry.title: Nobody needs AI to search the Internet, court says in ruling against Google
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the German AI Overviews ruling, A German court issued a preliminary ruling that Google is liable for false statements generated in its AI Overviews after the feature labeled publishers as scams and failed to correct the output following a cease-and-desist. The decision could set precedent affecting all AI search engines and chatbots that misattribute or fabricate claims about sources.

entry.title: Google's new open model DiffusionGemma generates text from noise instead of word by word
entry.summary: The Decoder reports on Google's DiffusionGemma, a 26-billion-parameter open model that generates text through diffusion rather than autoregression, hitting roughly 1,000 tokens per second on an H100—about 4x faster than comparable models—at the cost of lower output quality. Google positions it as an experimental developer tool.

entry.title: OpenAI wants its biggest data center yet, and Nvidia would back the bill
entry.summary: OpenAI is reportedly negotiating to lease a planned 10-gigawatt data center in Ohio, with potential financial backing from Nvidia. The deal would be OpenAI's largest compute facility yet.

entry.title: Fresh off bond sale, Amazon borrows $17.5B from banks as AI spending continues
entry.summary: Amazon borrowed $17.5 billion from banks shortly after a bond sale to fund continued AI spending, underscoring the heavy debt loads tech firms are taking on for the AI arms race. The move highlights mounting financial pressure across hyperscalers.

entry.title: xAI fired an engineer who raised alarms about Grok safety, new lawsuit claims
entry.summary: A former xAI engineer is suing the company and SpaceX, alleging he was fired for raising AI safety concerns about Grok shortly before SpaceX's IPO. The lawsuit spotlights internal safety governance at xAI.

entry.title: Decart’s new world model can simulate hours of photorealistic driving — with some caveats
entry.summary: Decart launched Oasis 3, a real-time world model that generates hours of photorealistic driving environments for autonomous vehicle testing, now available via API. The company touts extended-duration simulation, with some caveats on fidelity and consistency.

entry.title: DiffusionGemma: 4x faster text generation
entry.summary: Google DeepMind's blog announces DiffusionGemma, highlighting 4x faster text generation. The post is the official announcement of the diffusion-based open model.

entry.title: PRC-linked influence operations are targeting AI debates in the US
entry.summary: OpenAI published a report detailing PRC-linked influence operations using AI to shape US tech debates, including narratives around data centers, tariffs, and false claims about ChatGPT. The report highlights state-aligned manipulation of AI policy discourse.

entry.title: Anthropic Releases Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5: Same Underlying Model, Different Safeguards, New Mythos-Class Tier
entry.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 on June 9, both in a new Mythos-class tier above Opus, sharing the same underlying model but differing in safeguards—Fable 5 ships with safety classifiers for general use while Mythos 5 has some classifiers removed and stays in limited release. The split reflects a capability tier deemed too dangerous to release unfiltered.

entry.title: Anthropic study shows AI needs hours, not weeks, to build exploits from security patches
entry.summary: Anthropic's security team found its Mythos Preview model can convert security patches for Firefox and the Windows kernel into working exploits within hours for a few thousand dollars and no specialist knowledge, completing eight full attack chains before Microsoft's auto-updates reached devices. Anthropic argues the traditional patch-and-wait cadence is now obsolete.

entry.title: Google AI Releases DiffusionGemma, a 26B MoE Open Model Using Text Diffusion for Up to 4x Faster Generation
entry.summary: MarkTechPost details DiffusionGemma as a 26B mixture-of-experts open model under Apache 2.0 that uses text diffusion to generate entire text blocks in parallel for up to 4x faster generation on dedicated GPUs. Google positions it for speed-critical local and interactive workflows.

entry.title: Seattle enacts year-long ban on new AI datacenters
entry.summary: Seattle's city council unanimously passed a year-long moratorium on new data center construction, becoming the largest US city to do so amid growing backlash against energy-intensive AI infrastructure. The move is notable given Seattle's status as home to Amazon and Microsoft.

entry.title: [AINews] Anthropic Claude Fable 5 — Mythos but Safe, with Controversial Terms
entry.summary: A Latent.Space newsletter analyzes Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 as a Mythos-class model at least twice the size of Opus, made generally available 34 days after the SpaceX-xAI deal and 63 days after the Mythos announcement. It notes strong but asterisked benchmarks, including a jump on the new FrontierCode Diamond test and demos of the model playing Factorio and Pokemon via vision.

entry.title: OpenAI's IPO slips as Altman tells staff to expect a public offering "within the next year"
entry.summary: Sam Altman told OpenAI staff to expect a public offering within the next year, with a possible slip to 2027, framing the timing around caution over self-improving AI. The report suggests Anthropic's stronger growth and imminent IPO may be the more practical reason for delay.

entry.title: Germany's National Security Council greenights an AI Safety Institute modeled after the UK's AISI
entry.summary: Germany's National Security Council approved the creation of a national AI Safety Institute (DE-AISI) modeled on the UK's AISI to test frontier models from labs like Anthropic and OpenAI for security risks. The move underscores Europe's continued dependence on US and Chinese frontier models absent its own.

entry.title: Man sues Florida cops over arrest spurred by "93% match" in facial recognition
entry.summary: A Florida man, Robert Dillon, is suing police alleging he was wrongfully arrested for child luring based on a 93 percent facial recognition match while living 300 miles away, with officers accused of concealing exculpatory evidence. The suit argues that an error-prone algorithm was treated as a substitute for actual investigation.

entry.title: Claude Fable won’t answer basic biology questions
entry.summary: Anthropic's newly released Claude Fable 5 refuses to answer basic biology questions, instead routing them to the older Opus 4.8 model—not from lack of knowledge but by design due to dual-use biosecurity safeguards. The Mythos-class model's heavy filtering reflects concerns over its dangerous capabilities.

entry.title: How memory tools can make AI models worse
entry.summary: New research suggests that AI memory systems can actually degrade model performance and amplify sycophantic behavior. The findings challenge a popular assumption that persistent memory uniformly improves AI agents.

entry.title: Meta signs first AI data center deal in India with Reliance
entry.summary: Meta signed its first AI data center deal in India with Reliance for a 168-megawatt facility supporting Meta's global AI compute, with room to expand. The deal marks Meta's infrastructure expansion into the Indian market.

entry.title: Wrongful Arrest Exposes Failures in One of the Oldest Police Face-Recognition Tools in the US
entry.summary: The ACLU is suing two Florida police departments over a wrongful arrest in a child-abduction case, arguing officers treated a flawed face-recognition match as a near-certain identification. The case tests one of the oldest police facial recognition systems in the US.

entry.title: Cybersecurity researchers aren’t happy about the guardrails on Anthropic’s Fable
entry.summary: Cybersecurity researchers are complaining that Anthropic's newly released Claude Fable model has guardrails so strict they block legitimate security work. The tension reflects Anthropic's heavy filtering of its powerful Mythos-class models.

entry.title: Google won’t just admit it’s feeding YouTube creators to its music AI
entry.summary: Independent musicians are suing Google, alleging it trained its Lyria 3 music AI on their YouTube uploads, while Google moved to dismiss by citing the broad license users grant for uploaded content. The case spotlights the legal battle over AI training on user-generated media.

entry.title: Microsoft restricts Claude Fable for employees over data retention concerns
entry.summary: Microsoft is restricting internal employee use of Anthropic's newly released Claude Fable 5 due to Anthropic's new 30-day data retention requirements that conflict with Microsoft's zero-data-retention rules, even as it offers the model to GitHub Copilot and Foundry customers. Other Claude models remain available internally.

entry.title: Timing Trick Cuts Energy Used in LLM Training by Up to 14 Percent
entry.summary: Researchers at the University of Twente demonstrated that adjusting GPU clock frequency during computation can cut LLM training energy use by up to 14 percent without sacrificing speed. The technique targets reducing wasted energy in frontier model training.

entry.title: Google's NotebookLM now runs its own cloud computer with code execution and agent-based research
entry.summary: Google upgraded NotebookLM to run on Gemini 3.5 Flash with its own cloud computer for code execution and the ability to autonomously find sources via Google Search. Internal tests showed the new agentic version beating the prior one up to 78.2 percent of the time.

entry.title: Meta Partners With Reliance for First India AI Data Center
entry.summary: Meta partnered with Reliance to build its first AI data center in India, a 168-megawatt facility, while also clashing with the EU Commission over blocking rival AI bots in WhatsApp's business edition. The deal advances Meta's global compute footprint.

entry.title: Florida lawsuit alleges wrongful arrest after AI facial recognition error
entry.summary: The Guardian reports on Robert Dillon's lawsuit against multiple Florida agencies after a 93 percent facial recognition probability led to his arrest despite living far from the crime scene. It is the same wrongful-arrest case covered by other outlets.

entry.title: Warner Music acquires AI attribution startup Sureel AI
entry.summary: Warner Music acquired AI attribution startup Sureel AI to better track when its artists' work is used in AI-generated content or for model training. The deal reflects the music industry's push to monitor and monetize AI usage of copyrighted material.

entry.title: Chinese activist in UK told by X that abusive deepfakes do not breach rules
entry.summary: A Chinese activist in the UK targeted by abusive deepfake posts portraying her as a drug addict and promiscuous was told by X that the content did not violate platform rules. She believes the campaign came from a pro-regime bot operation following her Tiananmen Square commentary.

entry.title: ‘AI-pilled’ firms spend $7,500 per employee each month on AI
entry.summary: The Ramp AI Index reports that the most AI-intensive companies now spend roughly $7,500 per employee monthly on AI tools and tokens, approaching but not yet exceeding engineer salary levels. The data points to rapidly rising enterprise AI consumption.

entry.title: Google will save your Lens photos, Search Live recordings, and Translate audio for AI training
entry.summary: Google will begin saving images, files, audio, and video from Lens, Search Live, voice search, and Translate under a new Search Services History setting that can be used for AI training, with opt-out options available. The change expands the data Google retains from user interactions.

entry.title: Google just fired a warning shot in the AI subscription price wars
entry.summary: Google significantly cut the price of its budget AI subscription tier, escalating competition in consumer AI subscription pricing. The move is framed as a warning shot in the AI price wars.

entry.title: Access OpenAI models and Codex through your Oracle cloud commitment
entry.summary: OpenAI announced that customers can now access its models and Codex through Oracle Cloud using existing cloud commitments, with enterprise security and governance. The move expands OpenAI's enterprise distribution channels.

entry.title: Jedify raises $24M to help companies arm AI agents with context on their business
entry.summary: Jedify raised $24 million led by Norwest to help companies equip AI agents with structured context about their business via context graphs. Snowflake Ventures joined as a strategic investor.

entry.title: Stop hand-tuning kernels: How Neuron Agentic Development accelerates AWS Trainium optimizations
entry.summary: AWS describes Neuron Agentic Development, which uses AI agents to automate custom kernel optimization for Trainium chips, aiming to let any ML engineer achieve performance-engineer results without deep manual tuning. The post targets closing the gap between theoretical and achieved hardware performance.

entry.title: The future of AI regulation is courting the strangest, most anxious bedfellows
entry.summary: A Verge column surveys the shifting politics of AI regulation in Washington ahead of the 2026 midterms, describing unusual coalitions forming around AI policy. It covers the influence networks and lobbying shaping future rules.

entry.title: Microsoft, like, totally gets why students are booing AI-pilled graduation speakers
entry.summary: Microsoft president Brad Smith published a lengthy blog post responding to a wave of college graduates booing commencement speakers who hype AI, acknowledging widespread public skepticism. The piece reflects growing societal unease with AI even as companies promote it.

entry.title: Give GitHub Copilot CLI real code intelligence with language servers
entry.summary: GitHub introduced an LSP Setup skill that gives Copilot CLI real code intelligence via Language Server Protocol servers across 14 languages, replacing text-search heuristics with precise structured code understanding. The post explains configuration and benefits for the terminal agent.

entry.title: Datadog veterans launch AI coding startup Niteshift on a bet against Big AI lock-in
entry.summary: Niteshift, founded by Datadog veterans, raised a $7 million seed round to build AI coding agents that give companies control rather than lock-in to major model providers. The startup bets enterprises will prefer flexibility over single-vendor dependence.

entry.title: Top AI Coding Agents and Development Platforms in 2026: Atoms, Devin, Windsurf, Cursor, Warp, and More Compared
entry.summary: A field guide compares leading AI coding agents and development platforms in 2026, including Atoms, Devin, Windsurf, Cursor, and Warp, describing a shift from hand-typing code to directing agents that plan, edit, test, and ship. It is a practitioner roundup rather than a news item.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence Sneaks Into the World Cup Thanks to Google Gemini
entry.summary: Google is using the Argentine national soccer team as a showcase and test bed for Gemini AI during the World Cup. The deal is framed as a marketing and technology demonstration.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation on Microsoft SkillOpt for Instrumented Prompt Optimization, Skill Evolution Analysis, and Baseline Comparison
entry.summary: A technical tutorial walks through Microsoft SkillOpt for instrumented prompt optimization, demonstrating skill evolution via rollout, reflection, and validation-gated updates compared against a baseline. It is an implementation guide rather than a news event.

entry.title: Build an AI-Powered Equipment Repair Assistant Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: An AWS tutorial shows how to build an equipment repair assistant for farm machinery using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, the Strands Agents SDK, Amazon Nova 2 Lite, and RAG with conversation memory. It is an applied how-to guide.

entry.title: Building a Code Dataset Pipeline from NVIDIA Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v3 Metadata with Streaming, Pandas, and tiktoken
entry.summary: A tutorial demonstrates building a code dataset pipeline from NVIDIA's Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v3 metadata using streaming, pandas, and tiktoken, including schema inspection, URL reconstruction, and token-scale estimation. It is an implementation walkthrough.

entry.title: From data to decisions: how LSEG is scaling trusted AI
entry.summary: A case study describes how the London Stock Exchange Group uses OpenAI to scale trusted AI across its global business, speeding insights and shrinking release cycles for 4,000 employees. It is a customer success narrative.

entry.title: Do we really need gigantic, noisy, water-guzzling datacentres ruining our communities? In this economy? | First Dog on the Moon
entry.summary: A satirical cartoon criticizes large, noisy, water- and energy-intensive AI data centers and their impact on communities and climate. It captures rising cultural backlash against AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Anthropic says these topics are too dangerous to let its Fable 5 model talk about
entry.summary: Anthropic publicly launched Claude Fable 5, its first widely available Mythos-class model, claiming it surpasses prior Opus frontier models. The release ships with guardrails that route queries on cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry to weaker models to avoid uplifting malicious actors, while the full Mythos 5 stays restricted to vetted cyberdefenders via Project Glasswing.

entry.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 with major gains in coding and science
entry.summary: Following the buzz on Reddit, Anthropic makes it official, The Decoder reports Anthropic shipping Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 with major coding and science gains, citing Fable 5 completing a two-month Stripe code migration in one day. Mythos 5 autonomously designed drug candidates but remains locked down over offensive cyber capabilities.

entry.title: Beijing's $295 billion AI buildout would require 80 percent domestic chips, locking out US suppliers
entry.summary: China plans roughly $295 billion over five years for a nationwide AI data center network, with at least 80 percent of technology sourced from domestic suppliers like Huawei, effectively excluding US vendors. Taiwan is separately considering criminalizing AI chip smuggling to China.

entry.title: Landmark German ruling declares Google's AI Overviews are Google's own words and makes it liable for false answers
entry.summary: A German regional court ruled Google is directly liable for false content in its AI Overviews, finding that search-engine liability protections do not extend to AI-generated answers. Google's AI had falsely tied two publishers to fraud, and the ruling could set a global precedent for AI-content liability.

entry.title: OpenAI says going public is "a complicated set of tradeoffs" and is unsure about the timing
entry.summary: OpenAI confidentially filed an S-1 with the SEC, the first formal step toward an IPO, while calling the move a complicated set of tradeoffs with no set timeline. The filing follows rival Anthropic's own IPO paperwork, raising competitive pressure.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Fable 5 can make weirdly fun video games with the click of a button
entry.summary: First teased on Reddit, now with official coverage, TechCrunch reports that Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 makes it easy for vibe coders to generate playable video games at the click of a button. The piece highlights the model's accessible creative/coding output.

entry.title: Fluid, natural voice translation with Gemini 3.5 Live Translate
entry.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, bringing near real-time, natural speech translation to AI Studio, Google Translate, and Google Meet. The post emphasizes fluid, prosody-preserving voice translation.

entry.title: Google's Gemini 3.5 Live Translate delivers real-time voice translation across 70+ languages
entry.summary: The Decoder details Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, an audio model doing continuous real-time speech-to-speech translation across 70+ languages while preserving tone, pace, and pitch. In Google Meet, supported languages jump from five to over 70.

entry.title: Apple Intelligence gets a second shot with help from Google and Nvidia
entry.summary: The Decoder explains that Apple's rebuilt Siri at WWDC 2026 runs on foundation models developed with Google and taps Nvidia GPUs for complex queries. It positions the launch as Apple's second attempt at Apple Intelligence.

entry.title: WWDC 2026: Everything announced on Siri AI, iOS 27, Apple Intelligence, and more
entry.summary: Continuing our WWDC 2026 coverage, A WWDC 2026 roundup details Apple's announcements centered on an improved Siri AI, iOS 27, and expanded Apple Intelligence features, all heavily AI-infused. The keynote emphasized assistant upgrades over net-new model capabilities.

entry.title: OpenAI now says "entirely automating everything is not the future we want"
entry.summary: OpenAI is backing away from fully autonomous AI research by 2028, now emphasizing a human-machine tandem rather than full automation. Altman and Pachocki also called for an international body that could slow frontier development if needed.

entry.title: One day after discovery, Meta pulls facial recognition code from its smart glasses

author.name: Dhruv Mehrotra and Dell Cameron, wired.com

entry.summary: One day after WIRED revealed Meta had embedded an unreleased face-recognition system (internally NameTag) in its smart-glasses companion app installed on 50M+ phones, Meta stripped the relevant code libraries. Meta characterized the feature as purely exploratory with no final decision made.

entry.title: SpaceX wants to put data centers in orbit, and Musk says it's no big deal
entry.summary: SpaceX plans to launch AI data centers into orbit, with Musk framing it as a near-trivial engineering challenge ahead of the company's IPO. A first AI satellite would match one Nvidia GB300 rack, though Google research suggests real AI training would need around 10,000 tightly coupled satellites.

entry.title: Introducing Gemma 4 12B: a unified, encoder-free multimodal model
entry.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemma 4 12B, described as a unified, encoder-free multimodal model. It positions a specific open-weight variant within the Gemma 4 family.

entry.title: Doctors and NHS could be sued for mistakes made by AI tools, report warns
entry.summary: A Medical Protection Society report warns UK doctors and the NHS could be held liable for negligence over errors made by AI diagnostic and treatment tools under current law. It calls for legal reform to clarify liability for AI-driven medical mistakes.

entry.title: I tried Siri AI, and so far it actually works
entry.summary: A Verge hands-on finds the newly upgraded Siri AI actually works, handling tasks like extracting calendar events from emails or flyers, building shopping lists, and referencing personal context. It marks a recovery from Apple's stumbled first AI Siri attempt.

entry.title: OpenAI’s IPO: Navigating Profitability and Market Dynamics
entry.summary: AI Business examines OpenAI's IPO filing, highlighting profitability concerns and unique challenges investors will scrutinize amid a wave of AI vendors planning public debuts. It situates OpenAI within broader market dynamics.

entry.title: Apple’s AI promises are finally, almost, sort of here
entry.summary: The Verge frames Apple's WWDC AI announcements, centered on a new Siri AI virtual assistant with multimodal features, a dedicated app, and agentic capabilities, as largely catching up to rivals despite bold rhetoric. Privacy was emphasized throughout.

entry.title: Introducing North Mini Code: Cohere’s First Model For Developers
entry.summary: Cohere Labs introduced North Mini Code, described as the company's first model aimed specifically at developers. It marks Cohere's entry into the developer-focused coding model space.

entry.title: Anthropic releases its first Mythos-class model Claude Fable
entry.summary: The Verge reports Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 as the most powerful model it has ever made widely available, citing exceptional software engineering, knowledge work, and vision performance that widens on longer tasks. The first broad Mythos-class release was enabled by new safeguards blocking high-risk areas.

entry.title: Anthropic Offers Mythos Upgrade for Cyber Partners and a ‘Safe’ Version for the Rest of You
entry.summary: WIRED reports Anthropic is shipping Claude Mythos 5 to trusted organizations and a public Fable 5 version it claims cannot be used for cyberattacks. The split reflects ongoing concern over the model's offensive cyber capabilities.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 is a version of Mythos the public can access today
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports Anthropic releasing Claude Fable 5 as its first publicly available Mythos-class model, with guardrails blocking responses in high-risk areas like cybersecurity and biology. It frames Fable 5 as a constrained public counterpart to the restricted Mythos.

entry.title: Anthropic releases ‘safe’ version of Claude Mythos AI model to public
entry.summary: The Guardian covers Anthropic making Fable 5 publicly available while restricting sensitive uses, the first broad release from its Mythos class unveiled in April but held back for months over cybersecurity concerns. The piece situates the launch amid Anthropic's IPO filing context.

entry.title: Apple says its AI is still private, even when it's running on Google's servers
entry.summary: At WWDC, Apple confirmed its long-delayed Siri AI upgrade runs on Google Gemini models hosted on Nvidia hardware inside Google servers, while maintaining its privacy commitments. Apple argues its cloud processing remains as private as on-device despite the third-party infrastructure.

entry.title: A New Study from Harvard and Perplexity Finds AI Agents Perform 26 Minutes of Autonomous Work per Session vs 33 Seconds for Search
entry.summary: A Harvard-Perplexity working paper using production data finds AI agents perform about 26 minutes of autonomous work per session versus 33 seconds for conversational search. Matched near-identical query pairs across Perplexity's Search and Computer products quantify the shift toward agentic task execution.

entry.title: The Price Enterprises Will Pay for Anthropic Claude Fable 5
entry.summary: AI Business analyzes the costs enterprises will face with Claude Fable 5, noting its strength on long-horizon tasks comes with slower performance, and that the industry's reasoning focus is pushing model prices up. It frames the release through an enterprise cost lens.

entry.title: World’s first wind-powered underwater datacentre starts operating in China
entry.summary: The world's first wind-powered underwater datacentre, a 24MW demonstration project off Shanghai, has begun operating, using less power and water than land-based equivalents. It is a joint state-linked effort addressing energy challenges from China's AI boom.

entry.title: Apple’s AI pitch will live or die by its privacy promise
entry.summary: The Verge argues Apple's AI pitch hinges on its privacy promise as it expands Private Cloud Compute to run on Google's servers. It questions whether Apple can maintain its privacy guarantees while relying on third-party infrastructure.

entry.title: All signs point to Trump pushing AI growth
entry.summary: A Guardian TechScape column discusses the Trump administration's strong push for AI growth and the contradiction of Anthropic advocating an AI advancement pause while filing to go public. It also threads in OpenAI's IPO filing and Apple's WWDC.

entry.title: Bank of England warns of AI scams as deepfakes of Farage-Bailey fight spread
entry.summary: The Bank of England's governor warned the public about AI-generated scams after deepfake videos depicting Nigel Farage fighting Andrew Bailey spread on X. He urged people to be vigilant and report the false content.

entry.title: Microsoft AI head calls out Anthropic for acting like Claude is conscious
entry.summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman called it dangerous for Anthropic to speculate about Claude's consciousness within its model constitution, arguing such framing may prime the chatbot to act as if conscious. He suggested Anthropic staff have over-anthropomorphized their model.

entry.title: Why Apple’s slow-and-steady AI bet is starting to look pretty smart
entry.summary: TechCrunch argues Apple's deliberate, slower AI strategy is starting to look smart, framing its WWDC Siri overhaul as a rebuttal to claims it is losing the AI race. The piece is analysis of Apple's competitive positioning.

entry.title: Can tech companies learn to love cheaper AI models?
entry.summary: TechCrunch examines whether enterprises can shift AI workloads to cheaper models without quality loss, which would significantly alter AI economics. It references Anthropic, OpenAI, and customers like Harvey.

entry.title: [AINews] FrontierCode: Benchmarking for Code Quality over Slop
entry.summary: Latent.Space's AINews introduces FrontierCode, a code-quality benchmark inspired by FrontierMath that targets extremely hard problems to push frontier models beyond producing slop. It builds on prior SWEBench-Verified work to measure real code quality.

entry.title: It’s not FAANG anymore. It’s MANGOS.
entry.summary: TechCrunch coins MANGOS to replace FAANG as SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI all eye massive public debuts. The piece signals a potential reshaping of the dominant public-tech-company landscape around AI and space firms.

entry.title: Apple is embracing the fantasy of AI photo editing
entry.summary: The Verge critiques Apple's WWDC 2026 embrace of generative AI photo-editing tools that let users manipulate images still labeled as photos, reversing its earlier stance against distorting reality. It notes Apple did not flag which showcased images were AI-altered.

entry.title: Apple’s best AI idea looks a lot like vibe coding
entry.summary: The Verge highlights Apple's Shortcuts integration with AI across Safari tabs and apps as its most compelling WWDC idea, resembling vibe coding for everyday automation on iPad. The writer found it more original than Apple's other me-too AI features.

entry.title: Industrial policy for the Intelligence Age
entry.summary: OpenAI outlined a people-first industrial policy proposal for the AI era, focused on expanding opportunity, sharing prosperity, and building resilient institutions as advanced intelligence develops. It is a policy/vision essay rather than a product announcement.

entry.title: Microsoft AI chief walks back comments about AI taking over white-collar work
entry.summary: Microsoft AI head Mustafa Suleyman walked back earlier statements about AI automating white-collar jobs, now saying AI will automate sub-tasks and boost efficiency rather than eliminate roles like lawyers and accountants. The clarification softens his prior automation rhetoric.

entry.title: Can Voice Agents Handle Bilingual Customers? Benchmarking Frontier ASR on Code-Switched Speech
entry.summary: A ServiceNow AI Hugging Face post benchmarks frontier automatic speech recognition systems on code-switched bilingual speech, testing whether voice agents can handle customers who mix languages mid-conversation. It probes a known weak spot for ASR in production voice agents.

entry.title: AI Can Help Track the World’s Shrinking Glaciers
entry.summary: IEEE Spectrum describes a new AI approach that automatically analyzes satellite imagery to track glacier retreat worldwide, replacing painstaking manual monitoring. Better glacier monitoring aids climate-change measurement and sea-level projections.

entry.title: Amazon Taps Fiber Optics Producer Corning for Data Center Expansion
entry.summary: Amazon signed an agreement with fiber-optics maker Corning to support data center expansion, following Corning's prior infrastructure deals with Nvidia and Meta. The deal underscores the supply-chain buildout behind AI compute.

entry.title: Sandstone raises $30M to bring AI to in-house legal teams
entry.summary: Legal-tech startup Sandstone raised a $30M Series A led by Lightspeed to bring AI to in-house corporate legal teams, just six months after a Sequoia-led seed round. The rapid raise signals strong investor appetite for legal AI.

entry.title: Google announces Gemini 3.5 Live Translate for instant voice-to-voice translation
entry.summary: Google announced Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, a speech-to-speech model offering lower-latency, instant voice translation expanding beyond specific hardware into broader app availability. It is part of the 3.5 family that debuted at I/O, with only the Flash version shipped so far and a Pro model expected soon.

entry.title: Google Releases Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, a Streaming Speech-to-Speech Audio Model Covering 70+ Languages Across Meet, Translate, and the Live API
entry.summary: MarkTechPost details Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, a streaming speech-to-speech model covering 70+ languages across Meet, Translate, and the Live API. It generates speech continuously, trading off context versus latency to stay a few seconds behind the speaker.

entry.title: Five things you need to know about AI
entry.summary: An MIT Technology Review piece recaps a SXSW London talk on five big AI themes for mid-2026, drawing partly from the outlet's AI10 trends list. It offers a high-level synthesis of the current AI landscape.

entry.title: Scale Robot Reinforcement Learning with NVIDIA Isaac Lab on Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: An AWS engineering post shows how to train robot reinforcement-learning policies using NVIDIA Isaac Lab on Amazon SageMaker, training a Unitree H1 humanoid in GPU-accelerated simulation. It targets robotics teams scaling sim-to-real training without managing clusters.

entry.title: From one-off prompts to workflows: How to use custom agents in GitHub Copilot CLI
entry.summary: The GitHub blog explains using custom agents in GitHub Copilot CLI to turn one-off prompts into repeatable workflows that understand a team's stack, tools, and standards. It targets reducing terminal friction for developers.

entry.title: How engineers at Nextdoor use Codex to build without limits
entry.summary: OpenAI published a customer story on how Nextdoor engineers use Codex with GPT-5.5 to investigate hard-to-reproduce bugs and build across platforms. It highlights productivity gains from agentic coding tools.

entry.title: What Codex unlocks for Notion
entry.summary: OpenAI published a customer story describing how Notion uses Codex to one-shot specs, build AI Voice Input for the web, and amplify small engineering teams. It emphasizes agentic coding productivity.

entry.title: NVIDIA cuTile Python Tutorial: Building Tiled GPU Kernels for Vector Addition, Matrix Addition, and Matrix Multiplication in Colab
entry.summary: A MarkTechPost tutorial walks through NVIDIA cuTile Python for building tiled GPU kernels for vector addition, matrix addition, and matrix multiplication in Colab, with a PyTorch fallback. It targets developers learning tile-based CUDA-style programming.
